analysis: Reviewed ClusterService.swift base lines 912-1512 and head lines 1-472. The visible head hunks add a private `environment: [String: String]?` property and an internal init parameter with default nil. The comment says parts start from `partEnvironment`, falling back to this process's own environment. The patch excerpt is truncated, and head text only covers lines 1-472. So head 1131-1133, 1301-1302, 1428-1429 and 1448-1463 were not visible. These cover the approvalSetAside/serveLocally logic, part-start environment wiring, and removeEndedApproval. I could not evaluate whether the new environment feeds `process.environment` at part start, or whether it is inherited from the coordinator/user environment in a way that could leak or alter prefix-cache/kill-switch behavior (T-041 DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, TB-007). Base process launch (lines ~1419-1432) sets executable, args, stdin and log fds, and inherits the environment. The init is internal (not public), so external callers cannot inject an environment, and the default preserves existing behavior. No concrete regression is supported from the supplied evidence. Next pass should check the head diff for 1131-1133 (approvalSetAside conditions on serveLocally/save), 1428-1429 (process.environment assignment, whether secrets or DARKBLOOM_* env vars are filtered or forwarded), and 1448-1463 (removeEndedApproval changes, T-053/T-054 approval semantics). Coordinator-approval behavior, cluster-member registration and the ClusterControlCommandLock paths are unchanged in the visible text.
